claims.claim: The European Commission confirmed a limit of 350,000 hybrid electric vehicles a year from China, expected to halve China's market share from 6 percent to 3 percent from December.
claims.episode_span: limit hybrid electric vehicles imported from China to 350,000 a year from December
claims.source_title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year
claims.supporting_quote: The EU is to limit the number of hybrid electric vehicles imported from China to 350,000 cars a year, the European Commission has confirmed.

claims.claim: About 800,000 battery and plug-in hybrids are likely to be sold this year, and Chinese hybrid exports to the EU tripled to 6.7 billion euros in the first half from 2.2 billion euros.
claims.episode_span: About 800,000 battery and plug-in hybrids are likely to be sold this year
claims.source_title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year
claims.supporting_quote: China’s exports of hybrids to the EU tripled to €6.7bn (£5.7bn) in the first half of this year, from €2.2bn a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data.

claims.claim: Cars above the quota would be blocked in customs without tariffs; EU-assembled vehicles are exempt and EU companies making cars in China are not.
claims.episode_span: Cars above the quota would be held in customs rather than tariffed
claims.source_title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year
claims.supporting_quote: Any cars imported above the quota level will not be subject to tariffs, but will remain blocked in customs at docks in Europe.

claims.claim: Officials said China supports the quota and agreed to drop some auto-parts tariffs and halve duties on EU footwear, olive oil and ice cream, amid a deficit of about 1 billion pounds a day.
claims.episode_span: China fully supports the quota and has agreed to drop some tariffs on auto parts
claims.source_title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year
claims.supporting_quote: As part of the deal, China has also agreed to drop some tariffs on auto parts and cut duties by half on footwear, olive oil and ice-cream from the EU.

John Sauer defended the FCC’s handling of a challenge to a Public Notice issued in March, which allows qualifying political party ads and certain joint fundraising committees to receive discounted rates traditionally reserved for political candidates.
